prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Predictions were consistently too high across all tests, as none produced statistically significant improvements.
Adding new screens (such as desktop controls quick-guides before finish) showed no clear effect.
Updating sign-in copy with cloud save security details showed no clear effect.
Adding photo quality hints during adoption upload showed no clear effect.
Adding wait progress and time estimate indicators on the home screen showed no clear effect.

Measured so far, by kind of change (relative change on the target step):
- adoption, hint: -4.7% over 1 test(s)
- finish, new_screen: -9.1% over 1 test(s)
- home, wait_info: +0.4% over 1 test(s)
- sign_in, copy: -4.0% over 1 test(s)

Funnel:
- choose_path: 76.2%, median 8s / mean 514s
- sign_in: 72.9%, median 3s / mean 567s
- adoption: 60.9%, median 89s / mean 1017s
- home: 81.3%, median 201s / mean 2336s
- finish: 64.8%, median 395s / mean 5815s
- finishing onboarding overall: 17.8%

Return JSON {"scores": [{"index": i, "impact": n, "evidence": n, "confidence": n, "cost": n,
"predicted_lift": x, "note": short}]}

Changes:
0: [sign_in, reorder] Move Sign-In After Adoption Certificate: Move sign-in after pet selection and adoption certificate generation so users customize their pet before creating an account. (why: Sign-in drops 27.1% of users early and adoption drops 39.1%. Allowing users to build emotional attachment first increases account creation motivation.)
1: [adoption, redesign] Split-Screen Companion Persona Selector: Redesign the pet selection screen into a split layout showcasing side-by-side animated pet previews and personality choices. (why: Adoption has the lowest conversion rate in the funnel (60.9%) and long completion times (89s median / 1017s mean).)
2: [home, new_screen] Desktop Visibility & Permission Verification Screen: Add a dedicated verification screen after waiting to check desktop rendering and prompt for window permissions before completing setup. (why: Support receives multiple reports of pets failing to display on desktop or the app stalling right after generation.)
3: [home, notification] Background Processing Desktop Alert System: Enable native desktop notification triggers on the waiting screen so users are notified when pet setup finishes while minimized. (why: The waiting step has extremely high mean time (2336s / 38 mins) and 201s median time, leading to dropoff while waiting.)
4: [choose_path, new_screen] Interactive Path Preview Screen: Add an introductory path preview screen illustrating the difference between ready-made adoption and custom pet creation. (why: Mean time on path selection is high (514s) and custom creation generation issues generate support tickets.)
5: [finish, layout] Desktop Controls Setup Checklist: Reformat home_intro to a checklist layout detailing core interactions like dragging, hiding, and chatting with the pet. (why: Support mail shows confusion on controlling, hiding, or talking to pets after completing onboarding.)
6: [home, wait_info] Hatching Companion Audio Visualizer: Add an animated hatching mascot and sound effects to the waiting screen during pet generation. (why: Waiting step takes median 201s / mean 2336s, causing user impatience and dropoff.)

scores.note: Delays sign-in until after emotional attachment, targeting major funnel dropoffs.
Redesigns adoption step which has the lowest conversion rate (60.9%).
Backed by support mail, but adding new screens has historically performed poorly.
Addresses extreme wait times (2336s mean) by alerting users while minimized.
Supported by funnel and support tickets, but adding introductory screens failed in past tests.
Addresses finish dropoff (35.2%) and support mail via existing screen reformatting.
Previous wait info tests yielded no statistically significant improvement (+0.4%).
